summary: This informational document records the IANA registration for the object identifier range donated by DigiCert for the Curdle working group's cryptographic algorithms. The range allowed shorter values for the Edwards curve key agreement and signature algorithms than other available ranges.

eli5.summary: A company gave a list of short ID numbers, and this records who owns the list and what it is for.

subtitle: A donated range of cryptographic algorithm identifiers for Edwards curves.

tldr.problem: The Curdle working group needed short identifiers for new Edwards curve cryptographic algorithms, but existing registries had longer values.
tldr.mechanism: DigiCert donated a range of object identifiers (from 1.3.101.100 to 1.3.101.127) for Edwards curves, and this document transfers control of that range to IANA.
tldr.outcome: The range is now registered with IANA, with assignments established for X25519, X448, Ed25519, and Ed448, and a specification-required policy for future allocations.

today: RFC 8411 is an Informational Internet Standard. The OID range is managed by IANA and remains the standard registry for Edwards curve algorithm identifiers.

sections.title: The Donated OID Range
sections.content: When the Curdle Security Working Group was chartered to standardize Edwards Elliptic Curve algorithms, they needed identifiers to distinguish these algorithms in protocols using Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1). DigiCert, Inc. donated a range of object identifiers (OIDs) for this purpose. This range, from 1.3.101.100 to 1.3.101.127, allowed Edwards curve algorithms to have shorter values than they would have using the existing S/MIME or PKIX registries. The initial registrations included X25519, X448, Ed25519, and Ed448 algorithms defined in RFC 8410.
sections.eli5: An important company gave some short numbers to use as names for new types of cryptography. The numbers had already been assigned to some of the new algorithms.

sections.title: IANA Registry and Allocation Policy
sections.content: This document transfers control of the donated range to IANA and creates the "SMI Security for Cryptographic Algorithms" registry. The decimal values 0-99 and 128 and above are retained by DigiCert. Within the usable range (100-127), value 100 is reserved for potential future child registries. Values 110-115 have been assigned to the initial Edwards curve algorithms and reserved for related algorithms. The allocation policy for any new registrations is "Specification Required", meaning that IANA will assign values only when supported by a published specification and evaluated by designated experts.
sections.eli5: The internet organization (IANA) now manages the list and decides who gets new numbers. To get a new number, you have to write down what you want to use it for and have experts agree it is a good idea.

sections.title: Security Notes
sections.content: This document registers identifiers but does not define the algorithms themselves. The security considerations come from the protocols that use these identifiers. The algorithms identified (such as X25519 and Ed25519) are defined in other RFCs and include their own security analysis.
sections.eli5: This paper just keeps track of the ID numbers. The actual security of the locks and keys comes from how they are designed, which other papers explain.
